recognize_zh: 鐵染色中，許多紅色核的紅血球系前驅細胞核周圍有多顆藍色鐵顆粒，數顆細胞（如右下成群的母紅血球）顆粒環繞核周三分之一以上，形成環狀鐵粒母細胞；背景紅血球大小形狀差異大，符合鐵粒母細胞性貧血。
features: Numerous erythroid precursors with small round nuclei highlighted by nuclear fast red
Blue siderotic granules in a perinuclear arrangement, encircling one-third or more of the nucleus in several cells (ring sideroblasts)
Clusters of adjacent ringed erythroid precursors in the lower right field
Other precursors with fewer scattered granules; larger myeloid cells lack iron
Background red cells show anisopoikilocytosis with elongated and teardrop forms
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear stained with Prussian blue (nuclear fast red counterstain) shows numerous erythroid precursors containing blue iron granules. In a substantial proportion of precursors the granules are coarse and arranged in a perinuclear distribution encircling at least one-third of the nucleus, satisfying criteria for ring sideroblasts, while other precursors show only scattered granules; larger myeloid precursors are iron-negative. The background red cells show anisopoikilocytosis. Findings are consistent with increased ring sideroblasts, supporting sideroblastic anemia in this clinical context.

ddx.dx: MDS with ring sideroblasts / SF3B1 mutation
ddx.vs: Iron stain appearance is the same; separated by age, dysplasia in other lineages, and SF3B1 mutation rather than germline ALAS2 or SLC25A38 variants.

ddx.dx: Toxic/nutritional sideroblastosis (alcohol, copper deficiency, isoniazid, lead)
ddx.vs: Morphologically identical ring sideroblasts; diagnosed by exposure history and laboratory testing and reverses after removing the cause.
Normal or iron-overloaded sideroblasts contain granules scattered randomly in the cytoplasm without a perinuclear collar.
